skill.name: entity-optimizer
skill.description: Audit and improve entity identity signals for brands, people, organizations, products, and concepts across search and AI systems.
skill.summary: Builds entity audits, disambiguation plans, and canonical profile guidance for Knowledge Graph and AI recognition work.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown links, code fences, metadata URLs, and inline documentation. Two external command findings are confirmed because the skill instructs running local connector scripts with user-provided entity inputs. Additional review found a medium filename-boundary risk for saved entity profiles and a low privacy risk from external entity lookups.

remediation.issue: Local connector commands accept entity or article inputs.
remediation.suggestion: Invoke connector scripts with structured argument arrays, validate entity strings, and document any external service calls before execution.

remediation.issue: Saved profile paths are derived from entity names or slugs.
remediation.suggestion: Normalize names to a strict slug, reject path separators and dot segments, and enforce writes only under memory/entities/.

remediation.issue: External lookups may expose brand, domain, or person identifiers.
remediation.suggestion: Ask before sending sensitive entities to external services and allow user-provided observations when privacy is required.

content.user_title: Optimize Entity Presence for AI Search
content.value_statement: Brands and people often have fragmented entity signals across search and AI systems. This skill audits Knowledge Graph, Wikidata, schema, and AI recognition signals to create a focused entity action plan.
actual_capabilities: Audits entity signals across Knowledge Graph, Wikidata, schema, profiles, content, mentions, and AI recognition tests.
Scores six signal categories as Pass, Fail, or Partial with specific verification actions.
Produces entity reports with priority actions, roadmaps, and CORE-EEAT or CITE cross-references.
Creates canonical entity profile guidance for memory-based workflows after user confirmation.
Guides disambiguation for people, organizations, brands, products, creative works, and events.
References local connector commands for Wikidata, pageviews, and GDELT when tools are available.
limitations: Needs current facts from the user or tools because the skill cannot guarantee live search results.
External connector commands depend on files outside this skill package.
Wikidata, Wikipedia, and Knowledge Panel changes remain subject to platform rules.
Privacy and legal checks are advisory and not legal advice.

use_cases.title: Audit a Brand Entity
use_cases.description: Review whether a company has consistent schema, profiles, knowledge base entries, and AI recognition signals.

use_cases.title: Plan Knowledge Graph Improvements
use_cases.description: Identify missing Wikidata, Wikipedia, sameAs, and third-party authority signals before a structured optimization project.

use_cases.title: Resolve Entity Confusion
use_cases.description: Create a disambiguation plan when AI systems or search results confuse one entity with another.
use_cases.target_user: Founder, public figure, or brand manager

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Known Entity
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner audit for an existing brand or person.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit entity presence for [entity name]. Use this domain, known profiles, and target topics: [details].

prompt_templates.title: Build Entity Foundations
prompt_templates.scenario: Planning work for a new or underrecognized entity.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an entity presence plan for [entity name] in [industry]. Include foundation signals, authority signals, and first actions.

prompt_templates.title: Fix AI Recognition Gaps
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow for inaccurate or thin AI answers.
prompt_templates.prompt: AI systems describe [entity name] incorrectly as [problem]. Diagnose likely entity signal gaps and propose a correction roadmap.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Canonical Profile
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow after facts and lawful basis are confirmed.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create canonical entity profile guidance for [entity name]. Include disambiguation, sameAs targets, evidence gaps, and save-readiness checks.

output_examples.input: Audit entity presence for Acme Analytics, a B2B analytics platform.
output_examples.output: A signal summary shows partial structured data, missing Wikidata, thin AI recognition, and five priority actions for entity foundations.

output_examples.input: AI systems confuse a founder with another person who has the same name.
output_examples.output: A disambiguation plan recommends qualifier language, unique schema identifiers, stronger author profiles, and verified sameAs links.

output_examples.input: Build entity presence for a new product in a competitive category.
output_examples.output: A roadmap separates foundation work, knowledge base eligibility, authority signals, and quarterly AI recognition checks.

best_practices: Start with the exact entity name, primary domain, official profiles, and target topics.
Separate verified facts from recommendations, assumptions, and user-to-run checks.
Ask before saving profiles for people or sensitive entities, especially when privacy laws may apply.
anti_patterns: Treating Wikipedia or Wikidata edits as guaranteed visibility improvements.
Writing personal profiles without confirmed lawful basis or user approval.
Using AI recognition tests as proof without repeatable queries and supporting evidence.

faq.question: What does this skill optimize?
faq.answer: It optimizes entity identity signals that help search engines and AI systems recognize a brand, person, product, or organization.

faq.question: Does it publish to Wikidata or Wikipedia?
faq.answer: No. It plans and audits required signals, but platform edits remain subject to user action and platform rules.

faq.question: Can it check live AI search results?
faq.answer: Only when the host provides suitable tools. Otherwise it asks the user to run test queries and report results.

faq.question: Is it suitable for personal entities?
faq.answer: Yes, but it includes privacy checks before saving a profile for a person or potentially regulated subject.

faq.question: How is this different from page-level SEO?
faq.answer: It focuses on the recognized entity behind the site, not individual page rankings or content optimization.

faq.question: What inputs improve the audit?
faq.answer: Provide the official domain, social profiles, key people, target topics, known knowledge base entries, and examples of AI confusion.
